plan: I will bid my value. This means my exit price will be my value. In the ascending clock auction, I will stay in as long as the price is below my value. If I bid lower than my value, I risk exiting too early and missing out on potential profit. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price that exceeds my value, resulting in a loss. Since this is the first round, I have no history to learn from.

[My value is $24. I want to win if the second-highest bid is less than my value. Therefore, I should bid my value, $24, in the sealed bid stage. This way, I will stay in the auction until the clock reaches $24. If the other two bidders bid less than $24, I win at the price of the second-highest bid. If at least one other bidder bids above $24, I lose, which is fine since winning would mean paying more than my value. ]

My value is $11. In the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the clock price is below my value. Therefore, I want to exit when the clock reaches my value. To achieve this, I should bid my value in the sealed bid stage. This ensures I stay in the auction until the clock reaches $11, maximizing my potential profit if the other bidders drop out before then.
